correctness.rationale: U_r={2^j−1}, V_r=2^r U_r are difference-unique Sidon sets: positive differences have unique 2-adic valuations and differ in range/modulus, making cross sums distinct. Hence all prescribed within/cross displacement coefficients are 0 or 1, graph simple, with A-displacement ±1 and zero A–B displacement ensuring connectivity. Exact Laurent factorization H_r(z)+rI=[u(z),v(z⁻¹)]ᵀ[u(z⁻¹),v(z)] is Hermitian rank-one PSD on the unit circle. Vector (v(z),−u(z⁻¹)) is a Laurent kernel, yielding a nonzero finitely supported eigenfunction at -r. The other fiber eigenvalue |u|²+|v|²−r is strictly below its z=1 value at z≠1, so not flat; -r is the spectral bottom. Independently checked integer difference sets, degree counts and compact-support residual for r=2..7. Universal result follows from symbolic valuation/identity.
residual_risks: Finite r checks not infinite proof; no uniform degree/hopping range claim.

value.rationale: An explicit parameter-unbounded counterexample family resolves a sharply posed two-site existence question in unweighted periodic graph spectral theory. Compact eigenmodes, spectral bottom and uniqueness are exact structural facts, not numerical curiosity; allowing long range is an honest parameter-dependent restriction.
residual_risks: Hopping distance grows exponentially and degree quadratically with r; not a nearest-neighbor or constant-degree theorem.

final_claim: For each integer r≥3 an explicit connected simple (2r²−r)-regular unweighted Z-periodic graph with two vertex orbits has a single flat adjacency band at spectral bottom -r and a compactly supported eigenfunction; hopping range and degree grow with r.
limitations: Fixed two-site periodic graph but degree and hopping range depend on r; no claim about positive energies, uniform gaps or nearest-neighbor realizability. Finite checks support the symbolic all-r Laurent proof.
